solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: They would be very different from carping, yes?

definitions.text: They would be very different from carping, yes?

indicators.note: letters very different from their printed order are rearranged, so the two words get shuffled

explanation.surface: A sardonic remark that some things are the opposite of moaning, isn't that right?
explanation.walkthrough: 'very different from' rearranges CARPING and YES together; the whole clue then describes the result, since speeches of praise are the opposite of carping.
explanation.definitionFit: Panegyrics are formal speeches of lavish praise, the opposite of fault-finding complaint.

clue.text: Tablet for oral condition caused by bacteria?

definitions.meaning: an inscribed slab fixed to a wall, such as a memorial tablet
the sticky film of bacteria that builds up on teeth

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether there is a pill to treat a mouth complaint brought on by germs.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a commemorative wall tablet, and the bacterial film dentists scrape off teeth.

clue.text: One old silly blockhead

indicators.note: silly suggests letters behaving foolishly, jumbled out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doddery fool is called a dunce.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle is an informal word for a fool or a dimwitted person.

clue.text: My delight no longer conveyed in song

definitions.text: My delight no longer conveyed in song

parts.words: My delight no longer conveyed in song
parts.note: an old English ballad's lover sings that the lady was once his delight, but she has cast him off

explanation.surface: A singer laments that what once delighted them is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tudor ballad's refrain runs 'Greensleeves was my delight'; the song is a lament because the lady has cast the singer off.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional ballad is a lover's lament for a lady who was once his delight.

clue.text: Zestful organisation to help motorists coming to journey's end

parts.note: the RAC, Royal Automobile Club, is a British breakdown and motoring organisation

indicators.note: the end of the word picks out its final letter

explanation.surface: A breakdown service turns up when a trip is ending, full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming to' simply joins the pieces. The RAC is a British roadside-assistance club like the AAA.
explanation.definitionFit: Racy writing or style is lively and spirited, so zestful is a fair synonym.

clue.text: What a type of pill can prevent? The idea!

definitions.text: What a type of pill can prevent
definitions.meaning: the contraceptive pill stops a pregnancy from starting
a notion or plan formed in the mind

explanation.surface: A quip about the contraceptive pill, ending with an exclamation of realisation.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the start of a pregnancy and the forming of a plan or notion.

clue.text: Impure stuff about to be got hold of by tot

indicators.text: to be got hold of by
indicators.note: the small word is held by the word for adding up, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: to tot up is to add, giving a sum
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Some dirty substance is about to be grabbed by a toddler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a small child, but here it is a total. C (circa) goes inside SUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Scum is the layer of dirty froth or impurities that rises on a liquid.

clue.text: Deflation that's inevitable after mountain-top experience?

definitions.meaning: a loss of status or a let-down
after reaching a summit, a climber must descend

explanation.surface: After a spiritual high, the let-down is bound to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedown is a humiliating fall or anticlimax; literally, what follows a summit is coming down.

clue.text: Fellow being healed by me gets professional grooming

parts.note: a fellow is a man
the setter calls themself I
those being healed are ones I cure

explanation.surface: A doctor boasts that the chap they treated now gets a smart beauty treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Fellow being healed by me' as MAN I CURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A manicure is a cosmetic treatment of the hands and nails done by a professional.

clue.text: Youngster with a smell collecting handout

parts.note: the dole is British state unemployment benefit, a handout
a smell is a scent

explanation.surface: A smelly young person is picking up benefit money.
explanation.walkthrough: DOLE is the British name for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: An adolescent is a teenager, a young person between childhood and adulthood.

clue.text: Sign this writer on to go to extremes

indicators.note: the word on goes to the ends, surrounding the other piece

parts.note: taken as written
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A writer is urged to sign up for something extreme.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign or portent of what is to come.

clue.text: Bang on again after this has been successful?

definitions.text: Bang on again after this has been successful?

parts.words: Bang on again after this has been successful?
parts.note: a bang is a fringe of hair, which is back on the bald head after the treatment works

explanation.surface: Something so successful that it is spot on once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bang on' looks like 'exactly right', but a bang (chiefly US) is a fringe of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a lotion that claims to regrow hair on a balding scalp.

clue.text: Superior map produced by duke to show type of territory

parts.note: U means upper-class, superior, in British usage
a plan is a map or drawing

explanation.surface: A fine map made by a nobleman shows the kind of landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from a famous 1950s British essay on 'U' and 'non-U' speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Upland is high ground, a kind of terrain contrasted with lowland.

clue.text: Like the bearing of a lord?

definitions.text: Like the bearing of a lord?

parts.words: Like the bearing of a lord?
parts.note: bearing looks like posture, but here it is a device on a coat of arms

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a person carries themself like a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' suggests deportment; in heraldry a bearing is a charge on a shield, as a lord's arms would show.
explanation.definitionFit: Heraldic describes coats of arms and their charges, the bearings granted to nobles.

clue.text: The samurai flailing around in a somewhat inexpert manner

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase for an adjective; the answer describes such a manner

indicators.note: letters flailing around are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A warrior swings his sword about clumsily.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateurish means lacking professional skill, done in an unskilled way.

clue.text: Farmer who let loose with weapon

indicators.note: letters let loose are freed to fall in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A farmer who set an animal free was carrying a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A flame-thrower is a weapon that projects a stream of burning fuel.

clue.text: Approve of performance having cried terribly in the course of it

indicators.note: the jumbled word lands in the course of, within, the performance

parts.note: an act is a performance on stage

indicators.note: terribly signals the letters are badly disordered

explanation.surface: A critic endorses a show though they wept awfully during it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performance' suggests the show itself; 'terribly' is the anagram signal and 'in the course of it' the container, with 'having' a plain link.
explanation.definitionFit: To accredit is to give official approval or recognition to someone or something.

clue.text: Trapped? End's near possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests another possible arrangement of the letters

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, leaving the four letters

explanation.surface: Someone caught wonders whether the finish is close.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensnared means caught in a snare, so trapped is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Enforce tonic with difficulty? I may offer something to remove bitter taste

definitions.text: I may offer something to remove bitter taste
definitions.note: the clue speaks as the person, who sells sweets

indicators.note: the letters are forced together awkwardly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone forcing down a bitter medicine is offered something to sweeten it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tonic' tempts you towards medicine; the definition is the sweet-maker offering something sugary.
explanation.definitionFit: A confectioner makes and sells sweets, which take away a bitter aftertaste.

clue.text: Soldier locked in overturned vehicle — very sad

indicators.note: the soldier is locked inside the vehicle
an overturned vehicle in a down clue is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier trapped in a vehicle that has flipped over: a terrible event.
explanation.walkthrough: GI, a US army private, is a crossword staple; in a down clue 'overturned' fits the picture of a vehicle flipped upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic describes something deeply distressing, causing great sorrow.

clue.text: Fellows of great eminence, mostly in terms of intellect

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase for an adjective meaning relating to the mind

parts.note: fellows are men

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word is kept, losing its last letter

parts.note: eminence also means height, so of great eminence is tall

explanation.surface: Men of high standing are judged mostly by their brains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eminence' suggests fame, but here it means height: TALL, cut by 'mostly' to TAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Mental means relating to the mind and its intellectual powers.

clue.text: Second bean plant at top of pole?

parts.note: a runner is a climbing bean plant, the runner bean
a thing at the top of a pole is up

explanation.surface: A climbing bean has reached the top of its cane.
explanation.walkthrough: Runner beans are grown climbing up poles, which ties the pieces into one picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The runner-up is the contestant who finishes in second place.

clue.text: Celebrity with very little energy to suffer from fasting?

parts.note: a celebrity is a star
V is the little, abbreviated, form of very
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A famous person with hardly any energy because they have not eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve is to suffer or die from lack of food, as in a fast.

clue.text: Poor area with big business failure unending

indicators.note: without its ending, the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a slump is a sharp economic downturn

explanation.surface: A deprived district suffering an endless economic collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: A slum is a squalid, overcrowded urban district of poor housing.

clue.text: Challenge some newspaper advertisement that will be taken the wrong way

indicators.note: the letters run the wrong way, from right to left
some of the words, a run of letters inside them, is used

explanation.surface: A newspaper advert that will cause offence is disputed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes ERAD from newspapER ADvertisement; 'taken the wrong way' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A dare is a challenge to do something bold or risky.

clue.text: Worker brought in if things grind to a halt?

definitions.text: Worker brought in if things grind to a halt?

parts.words: Worker brought in if things grind to a halt?
parts.note: grind to a halt sounds like a stalled project, but literally millstones that stop grinding

explanation.surface: A troubleshooter is called when work stalls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grind to a halt' is literal: the mill's stones have stopped grinding.
explanation.definitionFit: A millwright builds and repairs the machinery of mills.

clue.text: See it come in, go out, change around

definitions.text: See it come in, go out

indicators.note: around signals the word turned round to read backwards

parts.note: to edit is to change a text

explanation.surface: Watching the sea come in and recede, transforming the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide is the sea's regular rise and fall, flowing in and ebbing out.

clue.text: One strange miracle church originally put down as 'fanciful'

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the church comes first

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: strange signals letters in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A single odd miracle was first dismissed by the church as imaginary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges MIRACLE into MERICAL; 'originally' puts CH first.
explanation.definitionFit: Chimerical means wildly imaginative or unreal, like the mythical chimera.
